newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to auction 15 pct of Sibneft Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: Russia to auction 15 pct of Sibneft Oct 25.

text.p: Russia will auction a 15 percent stake in oil company Sibneft on October 25 for 65.04 billion roubles and a minimum investment of $33.56 million, according to the Federal Property Fund's Reforma bulletin.
The tender, which follows another for 19 percent of the company held earlier this month, is open to foreigners.
The winner of the auction must make most of the investment within three years but the rouble equivalent of $2.2 million must be paid within three months to cover the company's overdue debts.
OAO Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompania is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil companies. Its main production unit is Noyabrskneftegaz NYGS.RTS NYGS.RUO, in which it holds a 38 percent stake.
Non-residents are restricted to a 15 percent stake in Sibneft.
The auction for the 19 percent stake was won last Friday by a company called Sins, with a bid exceeding the minimum $43.48 million starting price by $1.5 million.
In addition, Sins paid almost 82.38 billion roubles for the shares, which are not actively traded.
It is still not clear who is behind Sins.
ZAO Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK) and Stolichny Bank Sberezhenii won the right to manage a 51 percent stake in Sibneft in a shares-for-loans auction late last year.
Noyabrsknefetgaz's crude output last year was 20.35 million tonnes, compared with 22.68 million tonnes in 1994, according to an earlier issue of Reforma.
